doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Rickie Lee Jones and the slow 'Embraceable You'
summary: Rowe notes the intro is a demanding job. Pizzarelli tells of a demo session with Rickie Lee Jones who wanted a very slow 'Embraceable You'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: That’s not a good feeling if you’re supposed to set up the singer and it comes for their entrance and they can’t —

Right, no. You’ve got to know where you’re going to start. And you know there was, I mean I played years ago with Richard Davis, Carl Allen, Buddy Montgomery and myself and Ben Sidran for Ricky Lee Jones. And she was making a demo which would become a partial record of standards. And I remember she wanted to do “Embraceable You” and I played the first chord [scats] and she went [sings] “Embrace me.” And I went [scats] and she said, “What’s your hurry?” I was like what am I supposed to do? So it was a complete different learning experience. I was like okay I’ve got to figure out what the hell I’m going to — but she wanted everything very slow and you’d go oh boy.
